sb_prompt: PLEASE DISCUSS MUSIC.  CAN YOU FIND MUSICIANSOR TYPES OF MUSIC THAT BOTH YOU AND THE OTHER CALLER LIKE?
turns: Yeah, I was actually just driving by this record store downtown and saw some really cool jazz on the shelf. Have you ever gotten into that kind of stuff?

Oh wow, really? Yeah, I actually had a friend who got pretty into jazz a few years ago but she quit pretty quick because she said it was just too quiet for her, you know what I mean? And honestly, I'm kinda the same way sometimes with stuff that's too slow, I just want to get somewhere. But I will say, there's something about the trumpet sound that's pretty cool though. Do you have any favorites, or do you just like to stumble on stuff?

Yeah, I mean, I'm kind of all over the place myself. I'll be in my car listening to something super loud and then suddenly switch to this really soft piano stuff. I don't really have a reason for it, I just like having options I guess.

Yeah, I get that, but sometimes the quiet stuff hits harder than the loud stuff, like my friend said she felt like she was breathing when she listened to it, but I just feel claustrophobic. So I usually stick to things with a beat, maybe some pop or rock, unless it's for work where I can't have music at all. Do you ever have to go somewhere quiet where you can't listen to anything?

Yeah, I actually have to be in the house a lot for showings so I can't have music at all when I'm working, but on the weekends I'll just put on whatever I want. Do you like rock? I've been really into some indie bands lately, stuff that's got a bit of edge but not too aggressive.

Yeah, indie stuff sounds kind of fun actually, just as long as the lyrics don't get too dark, because sometimes it makes me think about all the stress I deal with at the pharmacy and I don't need any more of that right now.

Yeah, I get the stress thing, but honestly I think the indie stuff is usually upbeat enough to distract you from it, and I'm not really into dark lyrics myself, more like this one band I found last week that's got this really driving rhythm.

Yeah, I can see how that rhythm could be a good distraction, especially since I'm usually surrounded by people breathing heavily and needing their meds fixed fast, so having something loud enough to ignore that for a minute would be nice.
That actually makes sense, because when you're rushing around showing houses and people are freaking out about keys or deposits, the last thing you need is silence or something too introspective.
Yeah, that's exactly why I need the rhythm sometimes, just to not think about how long people are standing in the line.
That's the thing though, sometimes the rhythm just feels like it's pushing you forward when you actually need to stop and think for a sec, even if just for a minute.

Right, I guess I get that, but honestly, that kind of pushing forward is exactly what I need when I'm standing there holding a prescription and the lady in front of me is crying about her insurance denial.
I mean, that's the thing though, when you're holding a script and people are crying, maybe you need the quiet to actually process it instead of just getting pushed forward by the beat.
Yeah, I guess sometimes the quiet is the only thing that lets you actually breathe after holding someone's hand and telling them it's going to be okay.
Yeah, that's really heavy though, like, do you think sometimes you just need a wall up instead of something pushing you forward?
Yeah, maybe I'm just used to being the one pushing people toward a solution, but I guess sometimes you do need to actually stop and hear what they're saying before you can help them.
Yeah, I totally get that wall thing, like maybe you just need five minutes of nothing so you can actually hear what they're saying without everything just rushing past you.
Yeah, honestly, maybe I do need that quiet a bit more than I thought, especially when I'm trying to figure out the dosage for the little ones.
Yeah, that's probably why it works best, just having that moment where you don't have to solve anything immediately.
Yeah, honestly, maybe a little bit of that silence would help me actually hear what they're saying without everything just rushing past me, even if it's just for five minutes.
Yeah, exactly five minutes might be just enough to actually process what they're saying without everything just rushing past you, maybe just put on something with no words or something.
Yeah, I mean, instrumental stuff sounds perfect for that, no words to get in the way while I'm thinking.
Yeah, that's probably the best option, instrumental just gives you space to think without adding more stuff to deal with.
Yeah, you know, maybe some piano or just ambient noise, nothing with words at all, that would probably be good for that five minutes.
Yeah, that's probably why I keep coming back to jazz sometimes, even if I don't go as deep into it as my friend did.
Yeah, I think that's probably the only thing that would help right now, just something with no words at all.
Yeah, that's the thing about instrumental, it's just background to actually think, but I still can't resist switching back to that one song if I feel like I need to move a little bit.

Yeah, that's kind of the thing, there's this one song I heard on the radio that has no lyrics at all, just this really weird synth thing that kind of matched how I felt when the lady was crying, and for a second I almost thought, oh man, I need to hear that right now, but then it faded out and I just went back to helping her with the phone call.
Yeah, that's actually kind of weird that you went back to helping her even though that synth thing sounded like what you felt.

Yeah, I guess it's just that sometimes the music doesn't do enough to make the crying stop, even if it matches it, so I end up just... I end up just taking a breath and telling them we'll look at it again tomorrow.
Yeah, I get that, sometimes matching the feeling isn't enough to fix the problem, you just gotta get back to it and figure it out, even if it doesn't help right away.
Yeah, I guess sometimes you just have to put on your headphones and try to block it out until the next patient comes in, even if it doesn't match the feeling at all.
Yeah, but it's funny, that synth thing was the only part that stuck in my head even after the song stopped playing, like I couldn't shake the feeling of the crying woman for the rest of the day.
Yeah, that's the thing though, sometimes you just can't make it stop if you don't have something to replace the silence with.
Yeah, but it's weird, because I usually have that same song stuck in my head for days after, so I guess my brain just wants to sit with that feeling instead of pushing past it.
Yeah, but I guess I just always push the feelings away before I can sit with them for long, even if a song makes me want to.
Yeah, but maybe that's just how my brain works, I guess I just need to let the feeling sit there for a while before I can actually move on.
Yeah, maybe I just need to let it sit a little longer before I can let it go.
Yeah, maybe that's the difference, I guess I need to sit with it until it actually makes sense instead of just pushing it away until I can't take it anymore.

Yeah, maybe it's just that mine always gets stuck on the problem itself if I let it sit too long, so I probably have to force myself to just turn the music up a little louder until I can focus on the next person.
